In the first 2 quarters of the program (May-Oct. 2024), the conceptual design of the conformal tank for the truck, was done. In the next quarter (Nov-2025 through January 2025), the conceptual design of a tank to be tested at the end of Phase 1, was done. This is a smaller tank, and of a cylindrical shape. Following this, the detailed design of the Phase 1 test article had commenced. In Q2 2025, progress was made on several fronts: the preliminary design of the Phase 1 tank was completed. The detailed design of the composite tanks was almost done. Some aspects of the boss design and flange design remain to be completed. The manufacturer for the tank (using AFP) was down-selected and preliminary quotes obtained. The testing lab for the Go/No Go test (Task 7) was also identified and quotes obtained. University of Dayton Research Institute (UDRI) performed static and fatigue tests at ambient and cryogenic temperatures. They also performed thermal fatigue tests on the composite panels. In Q3, 2025, the design of the Phase 1 tank was almost completed. There was a revision in the design of the sealing approach, moving to spring-energized seals- which provide more control over the sealing process, and reduce compressive stresses induced in the composite tank from bolt tightening. Page 1 of 30 Approved for Public Release Preliminary analysis of sloshing of LH2 in the Phase 1 tank geometry was completed. The design of the inter-tank supports (which support the inner tank relative to the outer tank) was iterated upon, and the final configuration was determined. UDRI performed thermal, static and fatigue testing of two selected layups of tank composite material. Discussions with tank manufacturer NIAR were complete, including the work-scope and a PO was ready to be placed for tank manufacture, and composite materials procurement process was initiated. Mechanical fatigue tests at UDRI were underway. Program was terminated on Oct. 2nd, 2025 with immediate effect, and hence these actions did not move forward. 3.0 Project Objectives The objectives of this project are to design, manufacture and test a conformal, composite tank to hold liquid Hydrogen (LH2). The tank is meant for heavy duty vehicular transportation such as tractor trailers and construction vehicles. The table below shows a list of tasks as per the SOPO. It shows each task and the percentage of the task completed at the termination of the program on Oct. 2nd, 2025. Task 2.1 is to collate and document the requirements of the liquid Hydrogen tank in a truck, including structural, fatigue and safety requirements. Task 2.2 is with regard to determination of the fuel system configuration for a full-scale tank for a truck. Task 3 is about developing the conceptual design of the conformal tank, as a feasibility study for the final tank to be developed at the end of the program.
